title: Generating human intestinal tissue from pluripotent stem cells in vitro.
author: McCracken KW
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kqpcvvn
materials:
Our differentiation method represents a significant advance over previous protocols for
several reasons; 1) This is the first demonstration of differentiation of human PSCs into
intestinal tissue, 2) The protocol directs differentiation of PSCs through stages that mimic
embryonic intestinal development and is highly efficient, resulting in organoids containing
an epithelium, of which, more than 90% expresses CDX2 3) Three dimensional growth
results in intestinal tissue with both secretory and absorptive function, 4) Organoids contain
all of the intestinal epithelial cell types and similar architecture with villus- and crypt-like
structures, 5) Organoids contain a stratified mesenchyme and express markers of smooth
muscle and intestinal sub-epithelial myofibroblast (ISEMF) cells.
The method described herein does not rely on the inherent ability of ES cells to
spontaneously differentiate into all tissue lineages. Furthermore, this is the first protocol to
describe a defined set of growth factors that are required at each stage of differentiation to
mimic embryonic development in vitro.
Despite offering such great potential, this system is not without its limitations. For example,
the intestinal organoids lack several components of the intestine in vivo, such as the enteric
nervous system as well as the vasculature, lymphatic and immune systems. Additionally,
while all of the major epithelial cell types are generated in proportions similar to those found
in vivo, and there is evidence of crypt-like domains housing stem cells, the 3-dimensional
architecture is not as regular as is seen in vivo and the villus-like structures are variable from
one organoid to the next.
Regardless of these drawbacks we believe that this system has extraordinary experimental
utility for understanding and modeling human intestinal development, homeostasis, and
disease. Moreover this system provides a viable starting point for future efforts at
bioengineering human intestine.

Reagent Setup
Human Pluripotent Stem Cell lines (hESC and iPSC)
Grow pluripotent stem cells in feeder free conditions on hESC qualified matrigel as
previously described15 (National Stem Cell Bank Protocols, www.wicell.org). Briefly,
hPSCs are cultured on hESC-qualified, matrigel-coated nunclon delta surface plates (6-
wells) in a 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C. Cells are passaged onto new plates every 4–5 days
using dispase (1mg/mL), as described by National Stem Cell Bank Protocols,
www.wicell.org.
Dispase
Resuspend dispase in Advanced DMEM:F12 to a final concentration of 1mg/mL. Filter
sterilize using a Millipore filter sterilization tube, make 10mL aliquots and store aliquots at
−20°C for up to 6 months.
Aliquoting Matrigel for hPSC culture
Thaw hPSC qualified matrigel on ice, or overnight at 4°C. Chill sterile microcentrifuge
tubes in a microcentrifuge rack at 4°C for 1 hour prior to aliquoting matrigel. Aliquot
matrigel into cold microcentrifuge tubes and store at −80°C for up to 6 months. CRITICAL:
Matrigel will solidify at room temperature (20–25°C), so it is important to work quickly and
keep matrigel cold throughout the aliquoting process.
Matrigel coating plates for hPSC culture
Coat 6 or 24 well Nunclon delta surface plates with hESC-qualified matrigel as described by
manufacturer. Briefly, thaw matrigel on ice (final dilution is determined by the manufacturer
and is lot-dependent) and resuspend in cold Advanced DMEM:F12 media. Add enough cold
media+matrigel to the tissue culture plate so that the entire surface is covered (1mL/well for
a 6 well and 0.5mL/well for a 24 well plate). Incubate plates at room temperature for at least
1 hour prior to plating hPSCs, but plates can be stored at 4°C for up to one week.
CRITICAL: Matrigel will solidify at room temperature, so it is important to add matrigel to
cold media prior to coating plates.

steps.title: Prepare intestinal Matrigel aliquots
steps.instruction: Thaw a bottle of Matrigel on ice or at 4 °C, add B27 supplement to a final concentration of 1×, Rspondin‑1 to 500 ng · mL⁻¹, Noggin to 100 ng · mL⁻¹ and EGF to 100 ng · mL⁻¹, mix by pipetting, keep the mixture cold, dispense 50 µL aliquots into 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes and store at –80 °C for up to 6 months (growth‑factor‑supplemented Matrigel is optional but increases spheroid outgrowth).

steps.title: Reconstitute growth factors
steps.instruction: Reconstitute each growth factor in 1× PBS to the following stock concentrations: Activin A 100 ng · µL⁻¹, EGF 50 ng · µL⁻¹, FGF4 500 ng · µL⁻¹, WNT3a 500 ng · µL⁻¹, Rspondin‑1 500 ng · µL⁻¹, Noggin 50 ng · µL⁻¹; store stocks at 4 °C for ≤1 week, aliquot and keep at –80 °C for ≤6 months, after thaw keep at 4 °C for ≤1 week and never refreeze.

steps.title: Prepare media reagents
steps.instruction: Make all media fresh as indicated (store at 4 °C as noted).

substeps.instruction: Day 1 Endoderm Differentiation Media: RPMI‑1640 + 2 mM L‑glutamine + Pen/Strep (100 U · mL⁻¹ penicillin, 100 µg · mL⁻¹ streptomycin) + Activin A 100 ng · mL⁻¹ (no serum).
Day 2 Endoderm Differentiation Media: RPMI‑1640 + 0.2 % dFBS (vol/vol) + 2 mM L‑glutamine + Pen/Strep (as above) + Activin A 100 ng · mL⁻¹.
Day 3 Endoderm Differentiation Media: RPMI‑1640 + 2 % dFBS (vol/vol) + 2 mM L‑glutamine + Pen/Strep (as above) + Activin A 100 ng · mL⁻¹.

Mid/Hindgut Differentiation Media: RPMI‑1640 + 2 % dFBS (vol/vol) + 2 mM L‑glutamine + Pen/Strep (as above) + FGF4 500 ng · mL⁻¹ + WNT3a 500 ng · mL⁻¹ (make fresh on day 1 of induction, store ≤4 days at 4 °C).

Intestine Growth Media: Advanced DMEM/F12 + B27 supplement (1×; add 2 mL per 50 mL media) + 2 mM L‑glutamine + Pen/Strep (as above) + 15 mM HEPES + Rspondin‑1 500 ng · mL⁻¹ + Noggin 100 ng · mL⁻¹ + EGF 100 ng · mL⁻¹ (freshly prepared, store ≤1 week at 4 °C).
PBST: PBS + 0.5 % (v/v) Triton‑X‑100 (store at room temperature ≤6 months).
Immunostaining Blocking Buffer: 10 % donkey serum in PBST (prepare fresh, keep on ice).

steps.title: Coat 24‑well plates with Matrigel
steps.instruction: At least 1 h before passaging, add enough thawed Matrigel (from step 1) to each well of a 24‑well Nunclon delta‑surface plate to cover the surface, keep the plate on ice, and let the Matrigel solidify at 37 °C just before use.

steps.title: Passage hPSCs onto coated plates
steps.instruction: Transfer hPSCs from a 6‑well dish (~85–90 % confluent) onto the Matrigel‑coated 24‑well plate.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate mTeSR1 from the 6‑well dish; if spontaneous differentiation is visible, remove it with a tungsten needle or pulled Pasteur pipette.
Add 1 mL dispase per well, incubate 37 °C until colony edges lift (optimize per lot).
Wash wells 3× with warm Advanced DMEM/F12.
Add 3 mL warm mTeSR1, scrape colonies with a sterile cell scraper.
Collect colonies with a 10 mL serological pipette, triturate 3–5 times by expelling and re‑aspirating to break colonies into 1–2 mm pieces (≈5 000 pieces per well).
Plate the triturated suspension onto the Matrigel‑coated 24‑well plate at a 1:6 split (0.5 mL per well). Optional: place sterile plastic coverslips in wells before coating for later immunostaining.
Tap the plate 5–10 times to evenly distribute colonies, verify under a stereomicroscope, and incubate overnight at 37 °C.

steps.title: Grow hPSCs to 85–90 % confluence
steps.instruction: Maintain the plated hPSCs until they reach ~85–90 % confluence (2–4 days).

substeps.instruction: Day 1: Observe under a stereomicroscope; floating debris is normal.
Aspirate media and debris, add 0.5 mL fresh pre‑warmed mTeSR1 per well.
Feed daily with 0.5 mL fresh mTeSR1, monitoring confluence.
If colonies become too dense or too sparse, discard the plate and restart (density critically affects downstream differentiation).

steps.title: Induce definitive endoderm (DE)
steps.instruction: Treat confluent hPSCs with Activin A‑containing media for three consecutive days.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate mTeSR1, add 0.5 mL pre‑warmed Day 1 Endoderm Differentiation Media, incubate 24 h.
Replace with 0.5 mL pre‑warmed Day 2 Endoderm Differentiation Media, incubate 24 h (floating debris is normal).
Replace with 0.5 mL pre‑warmed Day 3 Endoderm Differentiation Media, incubate 24 h.
After the Day 3 incubation, wash cells once with Day 3 media lacking Activin A.
Optional: if cells were on plastic coverslips, remove the coverslip for immunostaining (see step 8).

steps.title: Immunostain DE (optional)
steps.instruction: Fix and stain cells for FOXA2 and SOX17 to assess DE efficiency.

substeps.instruction: Remove coverslip, place in a new 24‑well dish.
Wash once with 0.5 mL 1× PBS.
Fix with 0.5 mL 4 % paraformaldehyde, 10 min RT.
Wash 3 × 5 min with 0.5 mL 1× PBS.
Block with 0.2 mL Immunostaining Blocking Buffer, 30 min RT on ice.
Add primary antibodies (goat anti‑SOX17 1:500, rabbit anti‑FOXA2 1:1000) diluted in fresh blocking buffer, 0.2 mL per well, incubate overnight 4 °C.
Wash 3 × 5 min with 0.5 mL PBS.
Add secondary antibodies (donkey anti‑goat DyLight 488 1:500, donkey anti‑rabbit Cy3 1:500) plus Draq5 1:1000 in blocking buffer, 0.2 mL, incubate 2 h RT.
Wash 3 × 5 min with 0.5 mL PBS.
Mount coverslip with Fluoromount‑G and image; DE should be >85 % FOXA2⁺/SOX17⁺.

steps.title: Induce mid/hindgut differentiation
steps.instruction: Expose definitive endoderm to FGF4 and WNT3a for up to 96 h, changing media daily.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate existing media, add 0.5 mL pre‑warmed Mid/Hindgut Differentiation Media per well.
Replace with fresh Mid/Hindgut media every 24 h for 2–4 days.
Observe under a stereomicroscope; 3‑D spheroids should appear after ~48 h. If spheroids are absent, repeat the daily media change until they appear.

steps.title: Immunostain mid/hindgut (optional)
steps.instruction: Stain the epithelial monolayer for CDX2 using the protocol in Box 1 (replace primary antibody with mouse anti‑CDX2 1:500 and secondary with donkey anti‑mouse DyLight 488 1:500).

steps.title: Collect mid/hindgut spheroids
steps.instruction: Harvest approximately 50 spheroids per well and pool them for embedding.

substeps.instruction: Using a 200 µL barrier pipette tip, pick spheroids from each well under a stereomicroscope and transfer ~50 spheroids into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Aspirate remaining media from the wells and replace with fresh Mid/Hindgut media as in step 9.

steps.title: Embed spheroids in intestinal Matrigel
steps.instruction: Suspend collected spheroids in cold Matrigel and form a bead in a well.

substeps.instruction: Thaw one 50 µL aliquot of intestinal Matrigel (step 1) on ice for ≥30 min.
Allow the spheroid‑containing tube to sit upright for 10 min so spheroids settle.
Using a 200 µL barrier tip, transfer up to 50 spheroids in <25 µL total volume into the cold Matrigel (total ≤75 µL).
Mix gently up/down several times, avoiding bubbles.
Pipette the entire Matrigel‑spheroid suspension into the centre of a well of a 4‑well (or 24‑well) Nunclon delta plate; the Matrigel should form a bead.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C for 10 min to solidify the bead.
Add 0.5 mL pre‑warmed Intestine Growth Media to cover the bead.
Replace the growth media every 4 days or when phenol red turns yellow.

steps.title: Split organoids after ~14 days
steps.instruction: Passage mature organoids into fresh Matrigel to continue expansion.

substeps.instruction: Thaw one tube of intestinal Matrigel on ice for every 10–12 organoids.
Trim the tip of a 200 µL pipette to a 2–3 mm bore so organoids can pass without damage.
Using the cut tip, dislodge the Matrigel bead containing organoids from each well.
Pipette the bead up/down 3–5 times to free organoids from the Matrigel.
Pool all bead‑organoid‑media into a sterile Petri dish containing 10 mL warm Advanced DMEM/F12; use a tungsten needle or fine forceps to remove residual Matrigel fragments.
Under a stereomicroscope, capture up to 6 organoids with the cut tip and repeat the embedding procedure (steps 25‑29) to form new Matrigel beads.
Transfer no more than 25 µL total volume (media + organoids) into each fresh Matrigel bead.

steps.title: Culture split organoids (second 14 days)
steps.instruction: Maintain the newly plated organoids in Intestine Growth Media, changing media every 4 days.

steps.title: Long‑term organoid expansion
steps.instruction: Periodically passage organoids to maintain growth for up to 140 days.

substeps.instruction: After an additional 14 days (28 days total), thaw one tube of intestinal Matrigel per 3–4 organoids.
Repeat the dislodging and pooling steps (31‑34).
Under a stereomicroscope, cut each organoid in half with a sterile scalpel (hold with fine forceps or tungsten needle).
Capture up to 12 organoid halves (6 organoids) with the cut 200 µL tip and embed as in steps 25‑29.
Culture in Intestine Growth Media, replacing every 4 days.
Repeat this expansion cycle every 10–14 days as needed (successful up to ~140 days).
